cases.sentence: Наташе казалось, что еще когда она в ___ увидала князя Андрея в Отрадном, она влюбилась в него.
cases.explain: «первый раз» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: It seemed to Natásha that even at the time she first saw Prince Andréy at Otrádnoe she had fallen in love with him. It was as if she feared this strange, unexpected happiness of meeting again the very man she had then chosen (she was firmly convinced she had done so) and of finding him, as it seemed, not indifferent to her. “And it had to happen that he should come specially to Petersburg while we are here. And it had to happen that we should meet at that ball. It is fate. Clearly it is fate that everything led up to this! Already then, directly I saw him I felt something peculiar.”

cases.sentence: Пьер со времени бала чувствовал в себе приближение припадков ипохондрии и с ___ старался бороться против них.
cases.explain: «отчаянным усилием» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Since the ball he had felt the approach of a fit of nervous depression and had made desperate efforts to combat it. Since the intimacy of his wife with the royal prince, Pierre had unexpectedly been made a gentleman of the bedchamber, and from that time he had begun to feel oppressed and ashamed in court society, and dark thoughts of the vanity of all things human came to him oftener than before. At the same time the feeling he had noticed between his protégée Natásha and Prince Andréy accentuated his gloom by the contrast between his own position and his friend’s. He tried equally to avoid thinking about his wife, and about Natásha and Prince Andréy; and again everything seemed to him insignificant in comparison with eternity; again the question: for what? presented itself; and he forced himself to work day and night at Masonic labors, hoping to drive away the evil spirit that threatened him. Toward midnight, after he had left the countess’ apartments, he was sitting upstairs in a shabby dressing gown, copying out the original transaction of the Scottish lodge of Freemasons at a table in his low room cloudy with tobacco smoke, when someone came in. It was Prince Andréy.

cases.sentence: — А, это вы, — сказал Пьер с рассеянным и ___.
cases.explain: «недовольным видом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Ah, it’s you!” said Pierre with a preoccupied, dissatisfied air. “And I, you see, am hard at it.” He pointed to his manuscript book with that air of escaping from the ills of life with which unhappy people look at their work.

cases.sentence: — А я вот работаю, — сказал он, указывая на тетрадь с тем видом спасения от невзгод жизни, с которым смотрят ___ на свою работу.
cases.explain: «несчастливые люди» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Ah, it’s you!” said Pierre with a preoccupied, dissatisfied air. “And I, you see, am hard at it.” He pointed to his manuscript book with that air of escaping from the ills of life with which unhappy people look at their work.

cases.sentence: Князь Андрей с сияющим, восторженным и обновленным к жизни лицом остановился перед Пьером и, не замечая его ___, с эгоизмом счастия улыбнулся ему.
cases.explain: «печального лица» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Prince Andréy, with a beaming, ecstatic expression of renewed life on his face, paused in front of Pierre and, not noticing his sad look, smiled at him with the egotism of joy.

cases.sentence: ___, я вас прошу, вы не умствуйте, не сомневайтесь, женитесь, женитесь и женитесь...
cases.explain: «Милый друг» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I? I? What did I tell you?” said Pierre suddenly, rising and beginning to pace up and down the room. “I always thought it. … That girl is such a treasure … she is a rare girl. … My dear friend, I entreat you, don’t philosophize, don’t doubt, marry, marry, marry. … And I am sure there will not be a happier man than you.”

cases.sentence: Пьер был ___, перед которым он решался высказаться; но за то он ему высказывал всё, что́ у него было на душе.
cases.explain: «единственный человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Well, go on, go on. I am very glad,” said Pierre, and his face really changed, his brow became smooth, and he listened gladly to Prince Andréy. Prince Andréy seemed, and really was, quite a different, quite a new man. Where was his spleen, his contempt for life, his disillusionment? Pierre was the only person to whom he made up his mind to speak openly; and to him he told all that was in his soul. Now he boldly and lightly made plans for an extended future, said he could not sacrifice his own happiness to his father’s caprice, and spoke of how he would either make his father consent to this marriage and love her, or would do without his consent; then he marveled at the feeling that had mastered him as at something strange, apart from and independent of himself.

cases.sentence: Весь мир разделен для меня на две половины: одна — она и там всё счастье, надежда, свет; ___ — всё, где ее нет, там всё уныние и темнота...
cases.explain: «другая половина» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I should not have believed anyone who told me that I was capable of such love,” said Prince Andréy. “It is not at all the same feeling that I knew in the past. The whole world is now for me divided into two halves: one half is she, and there all is joy, hope, light: the other half is everything where she is not, and there is all gloom and darkness. …”
